citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), channel POz (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples) -- the SAME git-tracked vector the autocorrelation and PACF cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg_poz_s002r02) -> PhysioAnalysis::arYuleWalker(order=4): Durbin-Levinson recursion on the biased demeaned ACF (from autocorrelation()) to solve the Yule-Walker equations for the AR coefficients + innovation variance. The reference re-computes it with statsmodels.regression.yule_walker(method=mle) on the identical signal, via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The root is the POz channel numeric vector (shared with the autocorrelation and PACF cases). The AR(p) Yule-Walker fit solves the Yule-Walker equations from the biased demeaned autocovariance for the AR coefficients + innovation variance; the PACF cut-off (folded previously) chooses the order, and the fit yields a parametric AR spectrum complementing the Welch PSD. arYuleWalker is a NEW op (Durbin-Levinson on the biased ACF, building on autocorrelation/partialAutocorrelation) completing the ACF/PACF/AR-fit lane. It reproduces statsmodels.regression.yule_walker(method=mle) BIT-FOR-BIT for both the coefficients (max |diff| ~5e-15) and the innovation variance (~5e-13) (the biased/MLE convention; the adjusted/unbiased convention and base-R ar.yw small-sample variance correction differ by construction and are not the target). The fitted AR(4) is stationary (all roots of the AR polynomial outside the unit circle, min |root| ~1.09) with a negative lag-2 coefficient, and its parametric spectrum peaks in the alpha band (~10 Hz) -- a valid oscillatory generative model of eyes-closed alpha. HONEST: coefficients + variance are signal properties; the reproducible content is the bit-exact AR fit + stationarity.
